source: Rules of thumb used in first-pass real-estate arithmetic: property tax around 1.1% of value a year (US average effective rate), homeowner's insurance around 0.5%, maintenance around 1% (the '1% rule'), closing costs around 3% of price to buy, selling costs around 8% (agent commissions plus closing) to sell, an 8% vacancy allowance on rent, and a 30-year fixed term, private mortgage insurance around 0.6% of the loan a year while the loan is above 80% of value. Capital expenditure is held apart from maintenance at 0.5% of value a year, because a roof is not a repair; property management at 8% of the rent collected, counted even when you manage it yourself, because your time is not free; the 1% rule (monthly rent against price) and the 50% rule (operating costs against rent) as screens, never as verdicts; residential rental property depreciates straight-line over 27.5 years on the building only, with land taken at 20% of value.
confidenceNote: Every figure is a national rule of thumb; property tax alone ranges from under 0.3% to over 2% by state. The template shows which it used; the room lets the price and rate be changed, and the rest can be edited here.
note: Rates are decimal fractions of price per year. Guardrails: PITI over 25% of gross monthly income reads amber; a DSCR under 1.2 reads amber; cash after closing under the emergency-fund floor reads red. D-088.
